From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai

Date: 2026-07-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA redlines — liability cap for trade secret misappropriation

Marissa / Neha — forwarding Stellaris's request. Highlights: they want a carve-out to the liability cap for trade-secret exfiltration, uncapped direct damages, and a specific preservation / forensics workflow. Procurement deadline July 16.

My thoughts / proposed approach (high-level):
- Keep the overall liability cap in place for general claims (commercially necessary).
- Offer a narrow uncapped carve-out limited to proven unauthorized misappropriation of trade secrets. Trigger conditions must be well-scoped (e.g., demonstrated exfiltration or willful misappropriation).
- Require contractual procedures: 1) 48-hour notice to Redwood once Customer suspects exfiltration; 2) immediate preservation hold; 3) appointment of a mutually agreed neutral forensic vendor or, failing agreement within 72 hours, each party may appoint and the vendors will agree an initial scope; 4) forensics report with defined admissibility/chain-of-custody criteria.
- Remedies limited to direct compensatory damages and equitable relief; continue to exclude consequentials except where statutory remedies mandate otherwise.

I drafted a short redline (proposed_carveout_redline.docx) with sample language. Can you review and confirm legal acceptance of the precise trigger language and the neutral-forensic process? Also confirm whether Redwood would accept uncapped damages only where the neutral forensics report finds: (a) exfiltration of files labeled as Customer trade secrets, and (b) that the exfiltration was due to Redwood's unauthorized access or material breach.

If we can agree internally quickly, I'll send a clean proposal back to Stellaris with the preservation checklist and a list of recommended forensic firms.

Thanks — Mateo
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-11T11:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redlines — liability cap for trade secret misappropriation

Thanks for the summary and draft. I reviewed proposed_carveout_redline.docx. High level guidance from legal: we can accept a narrow uncapped carve-out but only under strict procedural and evidentiary safeguards. Proposed edits below — I'll paste the core changes here for quick reference. We should aim to keep the customer's comfort level while protecting Redwood's risk exposure.

Core edits (summary):
- Trigger: replace "willful misappropriation" with language tying uncapped liability to "intentional and material misappropriation of Customer-designated trade secrets, demonstrated by a neutral forensic examination and corroborating logs or forensic artifacts."
- Notice & preservation: Customer must provide written notice and documentation of suspected event within 72 hours of discovery; Redwood will preserve relevant system logs and provide a secure snapshot for neutral examiner.
- Neutral forensics: agree to a mutually selected neutral vendor. If parties cannot agree within 5 business days, each may appoint a vendor and the two vendors will select a third neutral to reconcile findings (costs split 50/50).
- Scope of uncapped damages: uncapped direct damages and statutory remedies (e.g., injunctive relief, statutory trade-secret damages) only where the neutral examiner concludes by preponderance of evidence that Redwood's conduct caused the exfiltration. No uncapped punitive or consequential damages.
- Confidentiality of the forensics report: handled under a protective order; Redwood may redact certain internal operational artifacts with prior notice.

I also recommend we include an exhibit describing the evidence-preservation checklist and an estimate range for forensic costs (I'll ask ops for a standard SOW template and rough budget).

If that all sounds reasonable, we can present as a compromise: preserve the cap generally, allow uncapped recovery only after neutral forensics confirm intentional/material misappropriation attributable to Redwood.

Marissa Cole
VP Legal, Redwood Inference

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Emma Liang <emma.liang@stellaris-health.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-13T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: limited liability carve-out + preservation workflow (Stellaris)

Emma — thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise proposal that reflects a middle ground between Stellaris's request and Redwood's risk tolerance. Key points below and redline attached (proposed_carveout_redline.docx + preservation_checklist.pdf):

1) Scope of carve-out: Uncapped direct damages limited to "intentional and material misappropriation of Customer-designated trade secrets".
2) Procedural triggers: Customer provides written notice within 72 hours of discovery; both parties preserve evidence; neutral forensics vendor appointed by mutual agreement (or, if no agreement, vendor selection process in the redline).
3) Evidentiary standard & outcome: Uncapped damages possible only where the neutral forensics report (with chain-of-custody) finds by a preponderance of evidence that Redwood's unauthorized access or material breach caused exfiltration.
4) Damages carve: Uncapped for direct and statutory remedies only. Consequential/indirect damages remain excluded. No punitive damages.
5) Cost allocation: initial neutral vendor engagement costs split 50/50; emergency vendor hold costs billed to the party that triggered the hold unless otherwise agreed.

Attachments: proposed_carveout_redline.docx, preservation_checklist.pdf, forensic-vendor-list.pdf

Next steps: if Stellaris agrees in principle we can: 1) finalize an exhibit with the preservation checklist; 2) insert the redline into the MSA and proceed to signatures (DocuSign link below); 3) include a short SOW for forensic work as an optional addendum the customer can pre-approve.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/orderform-2026-0791
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-stellaris-carveout

Would you like us to replace "intentional and material" with different wording? We tried to balance legal certainty and your GC's concerns.

— Mateo
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
